review_candidates.description: Senior Project Controls Manager – Data Center Infrastructure Location: Spartanburg, SC Employment Type: Direct Hire Reports To: Director, Infrastructure Enablement Industry: High-Performance Computing (HPC), AI Infrastructure & Data Center Construction Overview Our client, a rapidly growing high-performance computing (HPC) and AI infrastructure company, is seeking an experienced Senior Project Controls Manager to establish and lead cost management, financial controls, forecasting, and change management across a large-scale data center development program. The Senior Project Controls Manager will be responsible for implementing a structured, transparent, and auditable cost control framework across complex construction and infrastructure programs involving multiple contractors, EPCM partners, equipment suppliers, engineering firms, and service providers. This individual will ensure that project budgets, commitments, invoices, change orders, and expenditures are accurately tracked, properly authorized, and aligned with approved funding. The ideal candidate brings strong experience managing project costs on large capital construction programs and has demonstrated success developing scalable project controls processes in fast-paced environments. This is a hands-on project controls leadership position focused on building cost management discipline, improving financial visibility, and ensuring accountability across complex infrastructure projects. Key Responsibilities Project Cost Controls & Budget Management Establish and maintain a comprehensive project cost control framework, including cost breakdown structures (CBS), budget coding, cost allocation, and financial reporting procedures. Develop consistent processes to ensure contracts, purchase orders, commitments, expenditures, and forecasts are accurately assigned to approved project budgets and funding sources. Manage project budgets, cost commitments, actual expenditures, accruals, and remaining financial obligations across multiple construction and infrastructure contracts. Maintain detailed cost tracking and reporting across engineering, procurement, construction, equipment, commissioning, and other project workstreams. Identify budget variances, cost overruns, funding gaps, and emerging financial risks. Provide actionable recommendations to program leadership to improve cost performance and maintain financial accountability. Ensure project financial data is accurate, consistent, traceable, and audit-ready. Cost Forecasting & Financial Reporting Develop and maintain comprehensive project cost forecasts, including Estimate at Completion (EAC), Estimate to Complete (ETC), cash-flow projections, and contingency utilization . Analyze actual spending, outstanding commitments, approved changes, and anticipated costs to forecast total project expenditures. Partner with construction scheduling and project delivery teams to align financial projections with construction milestones and equipment delivery schedules. Prepare monthly cost reports, financial dashboards, variance analyses, and executive-level project performance summaries. Communicate financial trends, budget risks, cost exposure, and forecast changes to senior leadership. Establish standardized reporting methods that provide clear visibility into project financial health across multiple contracts and workstreams. Support capital planning, financial reviews, investment decisions, and audit requests. Contract Administration & Invoice Controls Review contractor and EPC/EPCM partner invoices, pay applications, and cost submissions to verify contractual compliance, approved funding, and alignment with reported project progress. Validate invoices against contract terms, purchase orders, approved commitments, completed work, and supporting documentation. Identify billing discrepancies, unsupported charges, duplicate costs, and expenditures exceeding approved authorization. Coordinate with Finance, Procurement, and project leadership to resolve invoice issues before payment processing. Maintain accurate visibility into contract values, commitments, billed amounts, remaining balances, and projected final costs. Support consistent financial controls across multiple vendors, equipment suppliers, construction contractors, and professional service providers. Change Management & Cost Risk Establish and manage a formal project change control process covering scope changes, contract modifications, change orders, and budget adjustments. Maintain a consolidated change register tracking proposed, pending, approved, and rejected changes. Evaluate the financial impact of changes and ensure appropriate documentation, approvals, and funding authorization are obtained before commitments are made. Partner with engineering, procurement, construction, and commercial teams to assess the cost implications of technical and schedule changes. Monitor potential change exposure, claims, contingency usage, and other emerging cost risks. Ensure changes are reflected accurately in project budgets, forecasts, contract commitments, and executive reporting. Develop recommendations for cost mitigation, contingency management, and financial risk reduction. Schedule & Project Controls Integration Work closely with the Senior Construction Scheduler to integrate cost and schedule information into a comprehensive project controls framework. Align cost forecasts with construction progress, procurement milestones, equipment delivery, and commissioning schedules. Identify financial impacts associated with schedule delays, acceleration, scope changes, and critical-path activities. Coordinate with technical leads to validate reported progress and projected remaining costs. Support consistent reporting of project performance, financial risks, and delivery impacts. Establish clear accountability for cost coding, invoice validation, budget changes, approvals, and financial reporting. Partner with corporate Finance to reconcile project cost records, accruals, forecasts, and approved funding. Improve processes for cost tracking and financial controls as the organization expands its infrastructure portfolio. Train project teams, contractors, and delivery partners on established cost management processes and reporting requirements. Maintain accurate supporting documentation for financial audits, investment reviews, and internal governance. Extend project cost management practices into operating budgets and service contracts as facilities transition from construction to operations. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration , or a related discipline. 5–7+ years of experience in project controls, construction cost management, or financial controls supporting large capital construction or infrastructure programs. Demonstrated expertise in project budgeting, cost forecasting, commitment tracking, cash-flow analysis, and variance reporting. Strong experience managing Estimate at Completion (EAC), Estimate to Complete (ETC), and contingency forecasts . Experience reviewing contractor invoices, pay applications, and change orders within an EPC or EPCM project delivery environment . Strong understanding of construction contracts, cost breakdown structures, change management, and financial authorization processes. Experience managing cost controls across multiple contracts, vendors, suppliers, and project stakeholders. Proficiency with construction cost management systems, project controls tools, and advanced Microsoft Excel. Experience developing financial dashboards and executive reports using Power BI or comparable reporting platforms . Ability to collaborate effectively with Finance, Procurement, Engineering, Construction, and executive leadership. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to financial accuracy and documentation. Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams, enforce financial controls, and drive accountability without direct reporting authority. Excellent communication and presentation skills, including experience explaining complex cost and financial information to senior leadership. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large-scale hyperscale data center, HPC, AI infrastructure, or mission-critical construction programs . Background working directly for a data center owner, developer, EPCM organization, or major construction contractor. Experience managing financial controls for multi-million-dollar or billion-dollar capital infrastructure programs. Familiarity with Primavera P6, Procore, SAP, Oracle Primavera Unifier, EcoSys, or similar project controls and cost management platforms . Experience establishing enterprise-level project cost controls, financial governance, and standardized reporting processes. Understanding of construction schedule integration, earned value management, and critical-path impacts on project costs. Experience managing owner-direct procurement commitments and major capital equipment expenditures. Familiarity with financial controls during commissioning, project closeout, and transition into facility operations. Professional certifications such as PMP, AACE Certified Cost Professional (CCP), or Planning & Scheduling Professional (PSP) . Ideal Candidate Profile The ideal candidate is a hands-on project controls and cost management leader with experience supporting large, complex construction programs involving multiple contractors, equipment suppliers, engineering firms, and delivery partners. They understand how construction budgets, vendor commitments, invoices, change orders, and project schedules interact and can establish the systems and processes necessary to maintain accurate financial oversight. This individual has successfully implemented or improved project cost control procedures, bringing structure and consistency to environments where financial tracking may previously have been fragmented or manual. They are comfortable reviewing EPCM invoices, challenging unsupported costs, evaluating change orders, managing cost forecasts, and translating project financial performance into clear recommendations for executive leadership. Most importantly, they have the technical and commercial judgment to identify cost risks early, maintain disciplined financial controls, and ensure every project expenditure is properly documented, authorized, and aligned with approved funding . This role is best suited for someone with a strong background in construction project controls, capital project cost management, or EPC/EPCM financial oversight—not someone whose experience is limited to corporate accounting, financial planning, or general project administration.
